knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.9
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly names the two acceptability tests in formal GLM goodness-of-fit checking and the question each addresses?
knowledge_checks.body: Select Pearson chi-square and LRT statement.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Pearson chi-square and LRT are formal acceptability tests with distinct comparisons. Coefficient interpretation is separate from aggregate acceptability testing.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Pearson chi-square for aggregate adequacy; LRT for likelihood or deviance comparison.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating coefficient interpretation as finishing acceptability tests.

choices.label: Pearson's chi-square test aggregates squared Pearson residuals against a chi-squared reference to assess adequacy of fit. The likelihood-ratio test compares likelihood or deviance of the fitted model to a relevant nested or saturated alternative.
Interpreting every coefficient in software output is the Pearson chi-square test; R-squared is the likelihood-ratio test.
Pearson chi-square and LRT are identical for GLMs with large samples; the names differ only by software vendor.
Acceptability tests apply only before fitting; after Fit clicks, formal tests are unnecessary.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.9
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You have a fitted GLM and want to judge acceptability. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Outline what each test compares; refuse coefficient-only.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Each test has a defined comparison object. Coefficient reading or residual plots alone do not replace formal acceptability tests.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Pearson chi-square aggregate adequacy; LRT deviance or likelihood comparison. Refuse coefficient-only.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting coefficient interpretation as finishing acceptability tests.

choices.label: Pearson chi-square: aggregate squared Pearson residuals against a chi-squared reference (adequacy of fit). LRT: compares likelihood or deviance of the fitted model to a relevant nested or saturated alternative. Coefficient interpretation is separate from acceptability testing; this question requires applying the formal acceptability tests.
Interpreting every coefficient in the software output finishes applying acceptability tests.
Pearson chi-square equals the deviance difference between M_full and M_reduced; LRT equals the sum of squared Pearson residuals only.
Acceptability is judged only by residual plots; Pearson chi-square and LRT are optional labels for the same plot.
